The '''1964–65 Bundesliga''' was the second season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[West Germany]]'s premier [[Association football|football]] league. It began on 22 August 1964<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=97368|title=Spielplan 1. Spieltag|date=5 April 2001|publisher=DFB}}</ref> and ended on 15 May 1965.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=97658|title=Saison 1964/1965 Letzter Spieltag|date=5 April 2001|publisher=DFB}}</ref> [[1. FC Köln]] were the defending champions.

==Season overview==
{{See also|Bundesliga scandal (1965)}}
The championship was won by [[SV Werder Bremen|Werder Bremen]]. [[FC Schalke 04|Schalke 04]] and [[Karlsruher SC]] were originally going to be demoted to the [[Regionalliga]]. However, the [[German Football Association|German FA]] became aware of irregularities regarding transfer fees, signing bonuses and player wages paid by [[Hertha BSC]]. A cash audit was ordered, and the evidence collected from there was enough to revoke Hertha's license. In order to avoid any legal battles over Bundesliga membership, the FA decided to expand the league from sixteen to eighteen teams, meaning Schalke and Karlsruhe were spared relegation. Since Berlin should have a representative in the league as well, [[Tasmania 1900 Berlin|Tasmania Berlin]] were promoted besides the winners of the promotion play-off groups for the 1965–66 season.<ref>{{cite book|last=Weinrich|first=Matthias|title=Enzyklopädie des deutschen Ligafußballs, Band 3: 35 Jahre Bundesliga, Teil 1: 1963–1975.|publisher=AGON Sportverlag|location=Kassel|year=1998|pages=38|isbn=3-89784-132-0|language=German}}</ref>

The 1964–65 season saw the debut of Brazilian players in the Bundesliga. [[Zézé (footballer, born 1942)|Zézé]] became the first Brazilian to play in the league when he fielded for 1. FC Köln against Hertha BSC on 22 August 1964 while [[Raoul Tagliari]] scored the first-ever Bundesliga goal by a Brazilian for [[MSV Duisburg|Meidericher SV]] against 1. FC Nürnberg on 21 November 1964.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.sueddeutsche.de/sport/50-jahre-bundesliga-die-sz-elf-der-vergessenen-brasilianer-1.1625844 | title = Die SZ-Elf der vergessenen Brasilianer | language = de | website = [[Süddeutsche Zeitung]] | date = 15 March 2013 | access-date = 16 February 2023}}</ref>

==Teams==
[[SC Preußen Münster|Preußen Münster]] and [[1. FC Saarbrücken]] were relegated to the [[Regionalliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[Hannover 96]] and [[Borussia Neunkirchen]], who won their respective promotion play-off groups.
